title: Chocolate bark with salted honeycomb
subtitle: thin sheets of dark chocolate with shards of cinder toffee and sea salt
excerpt: Chocolate bark is one of the simplest things to make and one of the most effective for gifting. Dark chocolate is melted, spread thin, scattered with broken honeycomb and flaky sea salt, and left to set. The honeycomb softens slightly into the chocolate as it sits, so the bark is best made and eaten within two days.
sourceNotes: Chocolate bark is a modern British and American confectionery technique widely documented in home-baking publications from the 2000s onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of melting and cooling chocolate through specific temperatures to stabilise its cocoa-butter crystals, giving it a high gloss and a clean snap when broken.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten within 2 days of making, as the honeycomb absorbs moisture and softens over time. Keep in an airtight box at a cool room temperature, not in the fridge.

content.text: chocolate will set with a glossy surface and a clean snap. If you skip tempering and just melt the chocolate, it will still taste good but may set with a dull or streaky surface. For bark, the difference is mostly cosmetic.

items.prepNote: broken into small irregular pieces (homemade or shop-bought)

content.text: Line a large baking tray or sheet with baking parchment.
Melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until completely smooth. The base of the bowl must not touch the water. Remove from the heat once melted.
Pour the chocolate onto the lined tray and spread it with a palette knife into a thin, even layer roughly 3 mm thick. Work quickly before the chocolate begins to set.
Scatter the broken honeycomb pieces over the surface, pressing them lightly into the chocolate. Sprinkle the flaky sea salt evenly over the top.

Leave to set at cool room temperature for at least 60 minutes until completely firm. Do not refrigerate, as condensation will dull the surface and make the honeycomb sticky. Once set, break the bark into irregular shards.

attrs.problem: Honeycomb has become sticky and soft
attrs.avoid: Avoid refrigerating the bark or storing it in a damp place.
attrs.fix: Make and eat within 2 days. Once the honeycomb has softened, the texture cannot be recovered.

attrs.problem: Chocolate has a dull, streaky surface
attrs.avoid: Avoid any water getting into the melted chocolate; even a drop causes bloom.
attrs.fix: The flavour is unaffected. For a glossy finish next time, temper the chocolate before spreading.
